\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صيد} (ṣayd)}{صيد (ṣayd)}]{\ar{صيد} (ṣayd) — hunting; fishing}

\label{lesson:AR-C536-sayd}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to fall out, then the Arabic for to abandon.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صيد}}
\textbf{\ar{صيد}} — \emph{ṣayd} — \textquotedblleft{}hunting; fishing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{يحب} \ar{خالي} \ar{الصيد} \ar{في} \ar{البحر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{yuḥibbu khālī aṣ-ṣayd fī al-baḥr.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My uncle loves fishing in the sea.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صيد}} (\emph{ṣayd}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-y-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to hunt, to catch\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Ṣāda, to hunt, and ṣayyād, a fisherman, which you know, share the root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣayd}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣayd}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{yuḥibbu khālī aṣ-ṣayd fī al-baḥr.} — My uncle loves fishing in the sea.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to fall out, then the Arabic for to abandon, then say \emph{ṣayd} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صيد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Hunting; fishing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صنارة} (ṣinnāra)}{صنارة (ṣinnāra)}]{\ar{صنارة} (ṣinnāra) — a fishing rod}

\label{lesson:AR-C536-sinnara}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to abandon, then the Arabic for hunting.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صنارة}}
\textbf{\ar{صنارة}} — \emph{ṣinnāra} — \textquotedblleft{}a fishing rod\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{نسي} \ar{أبي} \ar{صنارته} \ar{في} \ar{القارب}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nasiya abī ṣinnāratahu fī al-qārib.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father forgot his fishing rod in the boat.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صنارة}} (\emph{ṣinnāra}), a fish hook and a fishing rod, was borrowed from Syriac \emph{ṣenārtā}, \textquotedblleft{}a fishing gaff, a hooked tool\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣinnāra}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣinnāra}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nasiya abī ṣinnāratahu fī al-qārib.} — My father forgot his fishing rod in the boat.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to abandon, then the Arabic for hunting, then say \emph{ṣinnāra} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{اصطاد} (iṣṭāda)}{اصطاد (iṣṭāda)}]{\ar{اصطاد} (iṣṭāda) — to go fishing; to hunt}

\label{lesson:AR-C536-istada}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for hunting, then the Arabic for a fishing rod.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{اصطاد}}
\textbf{\ar{اصطاد}} — \emph{iṣṭāda} — \textquotedblleft{}to go fishing; to hunt\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{اصطاد} \ar{أخي} \ar{سمكة} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{iṣṭāda akhī samaka kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My brother caught a big fish.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصطاد}, \emph{yaṣṭād}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{اصطاد}} (\emph{iṣṭāda}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-y-d}, \textquotedblleft{}to hunt, to catch\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form VIII iṣṭāda, with t turning into ṭ, is to catch for oneself.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṣṭāda}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṣṭāda}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{iṣṭāda akhī samaka kabīra.} — My brother caught a big fish.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for hunting, then the Arabic for a fishing rod, then say \emph{iṣṭāda} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{اصطاد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To go fishing; to hunt\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استجم} (istajamma)}{استجم (istajamma)}]{\ar{استجم} (istajamma) — to unwind}

\label{lesson:AR-C536-istajamma}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a fishing rod, then the Arabic for to go fishing.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استجم}}
\textbf{\ar{استجم}} — \emph{istajamma} — \textquotedblleft{}to unwind\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استجم} \ar{أبي} \ar{في} \ar{القرية} \ar{أسبوعا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istajamma abī fī al-qarya usbūʿan.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My father unwound in the village for a week.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستجم}, \emph{yastajimm}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استجم}} (\emph{istajamma}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{j-m-m}, \textquotedblleft{}to rest, to gather again (of water in a well)\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Form X istajamma is to rest until one's strength comes back.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istajamma}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istajamma}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istajamma abī fī al-qarya usbūʿan.} — My father unwound in the village for a week.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a fishing rod, then the Arabic for to go fishing, then say \emph{istajamma} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استجم} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To unwind\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{استمتع} (istamtaʿa)}{استمتع (istamtaʿa)}]{\ar{استمتع} (istamtaʿa) — to enjoy}

\label{lesson:AR-C536-istamtaa}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to go fishing, then the Arabic for to unwind.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{استمتع}}
\textbf{\ar{استمتع}} — \emph{istamtaʿa} — \textquotedblleft{}to enjoy\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{استمتعنا} \ar{بالنزهة} \ar{كثيرا}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{istamtaʿnā bi-n-nuzha kathīran.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
We enjoyed the outing very much.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يستمتع}, \emph{yastamtiʿ}.

It takes \ar{بـ} for what you enjoy.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{استمتع}} (\emph{istamtaʿa}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{m-t-ʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}to enjoy, to profit by\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Mumtiʿ, enjoyable, which you know, is from the same root.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istamtaʿa}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istamtaʿa}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{istamtaʿnā bi-n-nuzha kathīran.} — We enjoyed the outing very much.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to go fishing, then the Arabic for to unwind, then say \emph{istamtaʿa} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{استمتع} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To enjoy\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
